firstPlayer: replaced by the role check: the Runner win rate in Expert against Expert
turnCap: none needed: the game ends after round 12 by rule (the Runner survives)
racer: none: there is no race in this game
agreementCountedOn: Expert decisions with 2+ sensible options, all Expert games, against Greedy for the same role

sanity.position: Hunter lethal: the Runner was just shown at a corner next to a pawn, both exits covered: move onto it
Runner don't blunder: shown at the centre, pawns two away: never end next to a pawn when a node out of reach exists
free Search: only two nodes possible, both out of every pawn's reach, only Searches in hand and energy that would cap anyway: Search one of them this round

report.summary: Dead on the role check, twice. The Runner wins 4.5% of Expert mirrors as specified (Sprint reach 3) and 7.5% after the one allowed rule change (Sprint reach 2); the band is 30-70%. Everything else passes: Expert beats Random 88.0% and Greedy 96.8% over 400 games each with roles alternated (as Hunter 100% and 99.5%, as Runner 76% and 94%); set positions 5/5; no caps (12 rounds by rule); Expert equals Greedy in 23.4% of 20,040 decisions. The Runner bot is not the weak link: as Runner it beats the Greedy Hunter 94%; it loses to a Hunter that uses its information.
report.loop: The Runner picks a move kind each round knowing the kind is announced; the Hunter narrows the possible nodes (announced kinds, Searches, Flares, reveals at 3, 6 and 9) and closes in. Watching Expert: the Hunter keeps the possible set to a handful of nodes with a Search or Block every round, and after any exact sighting it pounces; in the first run 25 of 37 catches were Sprints and 16 came with the Runner's node known exactly, mostly the round after a reveal. On a 4x4 grid two pawns sit within two or three steps of almost every node, so the Runner's choice of move rarely changes the outcome: a sighting ends the game instead of starting a chase.
report.ruleChange: Sprint reach 3 -> 2 (equal to the Runner's Dash), so that after a sighting the Runner could get out of reach and its choice of move would decide the chase. Runner mirror rate went 4.5% -> 7.5%: the grid itself, not the Sprint, is too small for two pawns with this much information.
report.notes: Expert is determinized flat Monte Carlo with paired samples (every action played out on the same redraws and seeds), honest on both sides: a Hunter, bot or page, reads only the public possible set, never the Runner. The spec's free-Search position was first written with a Block in hand, and Block on the right node wins 67% against Search's 48% there, so the position was rebuilt with only Searches in hand. The Expert also needed a dominance rule (never end a Hunter round leaving a free, informative Search unused when its energy would cap) because the Search's 3-point edge sits inside play-out noise.
